source_text: XII. Haec omnes de carcere simul scripserant, sed quia necesse erat omnem actum martyrum beatorum pleno sermone complecti, quia et ipsi de se per modestiam minus dixerant et Flavianus quoque privatim hoc nobis munus iniunxit, ut quicquid litteris eorum deesset adderemus, necessaria reliqua subiunximus. cum per plurimos menses reclusi tulissent carceris poenas et fame et siti diu laborassent, tandem sero produci iubentur et ad praetorium praesidis admoveri. et omnibus quidem gloriosa voce confessis, cum Flaviani adiutorium reclamaret amore perverso, negans eum diaconum, quod confitebatur in ceteros, id est Lucium, Montanum, Iulianum, Victoricum, dicta sententia est, Flavianusque rursum receptus est. et quamvis haberet plenam doloris materiam, quia scilicet de tam bono collegio separatus est, tamen fide et devotione qua vixit credebat: id fieri quod deus vellet, et tristitiam solitudinis destitutae religio sapientiae temperabat. dicebat etiam: Cum cor regis in manu dei sit, quae causa moeroris est, aut quare succensendum putem homini, qui hoc loquitur quod iubetur? sed de Flaviano postmodum plenius.
pass_a_gloss: Literal gloss: These men all wrote this together from prison, but because it was necessary to embrace every act of the blessed martyrs in a full account — since they themselves through modesty said less about themselves and Flavianus too privately laid this duty upon us, to add whatever was lacking to their letter — we have subjoined the remaining necessary things. After shut up through very many months they had borne the punishments of prison and had long labored with hunger and thirst, at last, late, they are ordered to be led out and to be brought to the governor's headquarters; and with all indeed confessing with a glorious voice, when the assistant of Flavianus cried out against him from perverse love, denying him to be a deacon, which confession he made for the rest, that is Lucius, Montanus, Julian, Victoricus, sentence was pronounced, and Flavianus was taken back again. And although he had full matter of pain, since of course he had been separated from so good a fellowship, yet by the faith and devotion in which he lived he believed that what God willed was being done, and the piety of wisdom tempered the sorrow of forsaken loneliness. He said also: Since the heart of the king is in the hand of God, what cause of grief is there, or why should I think anger should be felt toward a man who speaks what he is commanded? But about Flavianus more fully afterwards.
pass_b_english: All of them wrote these things together from prison, but because every deed of the blessed martyrs had to be set forth in a full narrative, and because they themselves had said too little about themselves out of modesty, and Flavianus had also privately laid this duty upon us to supply whatever was missing from their letter, we have added the rest that was needed.

After they had endured the sufferings of prison shut up for very many months, and had long struggled with hunger and thirst, at last, though late, they were ordered to be brought out and led before the governor's tribunal.

And while all of them confessed with a glorious voice, the assistant of Flavianus cried out against him from misguided affection and denied that he was a deacon, although he acknowledged it for the others, that is for Lucius, Montanus, Julianus, and Victoricus; then sentence was pronounced, and Flavianus was taken back into custody again.

And although he had abundant reason for grief, in that he had been parted from so noble a company, yet by the faith and devotion in which he lived he believed that what God willed was being done, and godly wisdom softened the sorrow of his forsaken loneliness.
He used to say: Since the heart of the king is in the hand of God , what ground is there for grief, or why should I be angry with a man who says only what he is commanded to say?
But about Flavianus more fully hereafter.

choices.english: to set forth in a full narrative
choices.why: ablative of manner with complecti means embracing the whole subject in speech, not merely completing a sermon
rejected: to complete with a full sermon

choices.why: ablative of motive; context is the assistant trying to save Flavianus by denying his rank, kindly meant but against the confession
genitive of description with tristitiam; he is left behind alone after his company is condemned
